 23|컴컴하고 습한 동굴이 아닌, 쾌청한 하늘과 낯익은 길드원들의 얼굴이 시야에 들어왔다.

 36|
 37|요즘 들어 약간 거리를 두던 송이 씨도 걱정스러운 얼굴로 물어볼 정도였다.
 38|
 39|“치유 마법이라도 걸어 드릴까요?”

 46|
 47|“……아, 네.”
 48|
 49|임꺽정이 귓가에 대고 속삭였다.
 50|
 51|“이 자식. 방금 같은 멘트는 도대체 어떻게 생각해 낸 거야?”
 52|
 53|“별로였어요?”
 54|
 55|“아니, 미쳤어. 듣는 순간 온몸에 전류가 흐르더라.”

 62|
 63|‘근데 왜 크리티컬 느낌이지.’
 64|

 68|
 69|“다들 도착하셨군요. 그런데…….”

 72|
 73|“혹시 무슨 문제라도 생겼나요?”
 74|
 75|“네. 너무 큰 문제라 이야기 좀 해야겠습니다.”
 76|
 77|단호하게 대답한 최 팀장이 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
 78|
 79|“진태경 씨도 함께요.”

 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|“스타 길드는 진작 왔고. 평화 길드는 왜 안 보여?”
 88|
 89|“잠깐, 저거 진태경 아냐?”
 90|
 91|“맞네. 옆에 원명훈도 있는 거 보니까 확실해.”
 92|
 93|“빨리 찍어. 잠시 후에 인터뷰 딸 준비하고.”
 94|
 95|최 팀장, 원명훈. 마지막으로 나.
 96|
 97|우리 셋은 구석진 곳으로 걸음을 옮겼다. 소식을 듣고 몰려든 기자와 헌터들의 시선에 얼굴이 따갑다.
 98|
 99|마침내 끈질기게 달라붙던 사람들의 시선이 떨어지자, 최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
100|
101|“갑자기 장소가 변경된 이유가 뭡니까?”
102|
103|“변경이라뇨? 그게 무슨.”
104|
105|“만티코어(Manticore)의 밀림이 오늘 레이드 장소 아니었습니까?”
106|
107|“예? 그럴 리가요. 혹시 지금 계약서 갖고 계십니까?”
108|
109|“여기. 정확히 명시되어 있습니다.”
110|
111|최 팀장이 건넨 계약서를 황급히 살펴본 원명훈의 얼굴이 와락 일그러졌다.
112|
113|“1팀장 이 새끼가.”
114|
115|반응을 보아하니 중간에 착오가 있었던 모양이다.
116|
117|평소답지 않게 몇 마디 욕설을 중얼거린 원명훈이 난처한 기색으로 말했다.
118|
119|“죄송합니다. 저희 쪽 직원이 큰 실수를 했네요. 이거 뭐라 말씀을 드려야 할지.”
120|
121|“실수. 그렇군요.”
122|
123|최 팀장의 건조한 목소리가 이어졌다.
124|
125|“오늘 레이드는 없던 것으로 하는 게 좋겠습니다.”
126|
127|“네?”
128|
129|“다른 곳도 아니고 A급 게이트입니다. 완벽한 준비 없이 진입했다가는 불상사가 생길 수도 있습니다. 그리고…….”
130|
131|짧은 순간, 말꼬리를 흐린 최 팀장의 시선이 나를 스쳤다.
132|
133|그는 이미 내 과거 행적을 조사했다.
134|
135|내가 3년 전 있었던 상동역 변이 게이트 사건의 유일한 생존자라는 것, 또한 그 후유증이 아직 남아 있다는 사실도 알고 있다.
136|
137|“우리 길드원들에게 와이번은 아직 무리입니다. 제의는 감사했습니다만, 이쯤에서 물러나는 게 서로에게 좋겠네요.”
138|
139|“팀장님!”
140|
141|원명훈의 당황 섞인 외침에도 최 팀장의 태도는 칼 같았다.
142|
143|“와이번은 안 됩니다. 적어도 지금은요.”
144|
145|“…….”
146|
147|가만히 상황을 지켜보던 내가 불쑥 입을 연 것은 그때였다.
148|
149|“하죠. 레이드.”
150|
151|“진태경 씨.”
152|
153|“인터넷 기사도 나갈 만큼 나갔고, 기자들도 모여 있는데 여기서 무산되면 뒷말 나오지 않겠어요?”
154|
155|나는 나란히 서 있는 최 팀장과 원명훈의 등 뒤를 빤히 바라봤다.
156|
157|어느새 목에 카메라를 건 기자들이 눈치를 보며 슬금슬금 다가오는 중이었다.
158|
159|‘냄새 하나는 기가 막히게 맡네.’
160|
161|심상치 않은 분위기를 읽고 접근해 오는 게 분명하다.
162|
163|그래서 최 팀장이 뭐라 말하기 전에 재빨리 말을 가로막았다.
164|
165|“그렇다고 제가 딱히 인터넷 기사에 신경 쓰는 건 아니고요. 그냥, 이제 괜찮아서 그래요.”
166|
167|“……정말입니까?”
168|
169|“네.”
170|
171|절반은 진심이고, 나머지 절반은 거짓이다.
172|
173|나는 아직 괜찮지 않다. 지난 3년 동안 늘 똑같은 악몽을 반복했고 놈의 포효와 팀원들의 비명을 기억했다.
174|
175|그러고는 식은땀에 흠뻑 젖어 깨어나 아무렇지 않은 척, 늘 똑같은 하루를 반복해 왔다.
176|
177|하지만 이제는 아니다.
178|
179|“할 수 있어요, 그때의 제가 아니니까.”
180|
181|나는 더 이상 무력하기 짝이 없던 F급 헌터가 아니다. 어디를 가도 당당히 강자라 말할 수 있는 한 사람의 절정 고수이자 A급 헌터다.
182|
183|“그러니까 해도 괜찮습니다. 아니, 하고 싶어요.”
184|
185|나를 빤히 바라보던 최 팀장이 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었다.
186|
187|“그래요, 그럽시다.”
188|
189|잠시 후, 우리는 불길하게 일렁이는 마력의 문 앞에 서 있었다.
190|
191|돌아가는 카메라와 쉴 새 없이 터져 나오는 플래시가 협동 레이드를 시작하는 양 측 길드원들의 모습을 담았다.
192|
193|“후우.”
194|
195|나는 깊은 심호흡과 함께 걸음을 내디뎠다.
196|
197|익숙한 시스템 알림과 함께 끈적한 마력이 몸을 휘감는다.
198|
199|띠링.
200|
201|
202|
203|- A급 게이트, [블랙 와이번의 둥지]에 진입하셨습니다.
204|
205|- 클리어 시 활약에 걸맞은 보상이 지급됩니다.
206|
207|
208|
209|스스스.
210|
211|다시 눈을 뜨자, 주위를 둘러싼 모든 것이 바뀌어 있었다.
212|
213|
214|
215|* * *
216|
217|
218|
219|“후욱. 후우욱.”
220|
221|두꺼운 통짜 갑옷을 걸친 임꺽정의 입에서 단내가 뿜어져 나왔다.
222|
223|게이트에 진입한 지 한 시간, 어느새 그의 이마에는 땀이 비처럼 쏟아져 내리는 중이었다.
224|
225|그것은 비단 임꺽정에게만 해당되는 사안이 아니었다. 스타 길드와 평화 길드. 도합 이십 명이 넘는 인원 중 대부분이 땀을 줄줄 흘리며 걸음을 옮겼다.
226|
227|‘그럴 만도 하지.’
228|
229|나는 혀를 차며 주위를 둘러봤다.
230|
231|이글거리는 태양 아래, 수십 미터가 넘어가는 나무와 괴상하게 생긴 풀들로 형성된 밀림이 끝없이 펼쳐져 있다.
232|
233|이처럼 보기만 해도 숨이 턱 막히는 광경에 습식 사우나보다 뜨겁고 축축한 공기는 화룡점정을 찍었다.
234|
235|‘원시림(原始林).’
236|
237|그야말로 공룡 다큐멘터리에 나올 법한 광경이 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있었다.
238|
239|날씨는 둘째 치고, 보이는 풍경 자체는 장관이라고 할 만했다.
240|
241|“이야.”
242|
243|나도 모르게 감탄사를 흘리고 있던 그때, 한 사람이 다가와 어깨를 툭 쳤다.
244|
245|“여유 있다, 너?”
246|
247|“아, 명훈이 형. 선두에 계신 것 아니었어요?”
248|
249|이동 대열은 선두가 원명훈, 중간이 나, 후미가 최 팀장과 김 집사다.
250|
251|내 물음에 원명훈이 하얀 이를 드러내며 씩 웃었다.
252|
253|“가끔은 뒤도 살펴야지. 다들 힘들어하는데 혼자 경치 감상하는 태평한 놈이 보이길래 와 봤다.”
254|
255|“이러다가 갑자기 와이번이라도 튀어나오면…….”
256|
257|“아직 밀림지대라 잡몹만 나와. 와이번 둥지는 절벽이나 봉우리에 있으니까 한참 멀었지.”
258|
259|“헐.”
260|
261|“와이번과 마주치려면 최소 반나절에서 재수 없으면 하루는 걸릴 거다. 경치 구경 실컷 해 둬.”
262|
263|상위 게이트일수록 장소가 넓어진다는 건 익히 알고 있었던 사실이지만 이 정도일 줄이야. 나는 혀를 내둘렀다.
264|
265|“대단하네요. 괜히 일주일씩 레이드 권한을 주는 게 아니었어.”
266|
267|“그만큼 오래 걸리니까. 너도 여기 같은 A급 게이트 몇 번 다녀오면 지긋지긋해질걸?”
268|
269|“글쎄요.”
270|
271|아마 그럴 일은 없을 것 같다.
272|
273|내게 있어 게이트라는 곳은 힘들고 지긋지긋한 일터가 아니라 더욱 강해지는 공간이 된 지 오래였으니까.
274|
275|“전 재밌는데요.”
276|
277|“……음. 뭐 그럴 수 있지.”
278|
279|묘한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보던 원명훈이 뭔가를 건넸다.
280|
281|“자. 갖고 있어.”
282|
283|“이게 뭔데요?”
284|
285|푸른 보석이 박힌 목걸이다. 아이템을 확인해 보기도 전에 원명훈의 말이 이어졌다.
286|
287|“냉기 마법 걸려 있는 거니까 걸고 있어. 너도 A급이니까 지금은 괜찮겠지만 나중에 가서는 체력 뺏긴다. 주요 전력이니까 힘 아껴 둬야지.”
288|
289|“형, 이런 거 안 주셔도 되는데요.”
290|
291|“주는 거 아냐. 대여해 주는 거니까 곱게 갖고 있다가 나중에 돌려줘.”
292|
293|척 봐도 엄청 비싸 보이는 물건이다.
294|
295|망설이던 나는 원명훈의 재촉에 어쩔 수 없이 목걸이를 걸었다.
296|
297|띠링.
298|
299|
300|
301|- [예티의 목걸이]를 장착하셨습니다.
302|
303|- 목걸이에서 설원의 바람이 흘러나옵니다.
304|
305|
306|
307|시스템 알림과 동시에 순간 등골이 서늘해질 정도의 한기가 전신을 휘감았다.
308|
309|“효과 좋네요.”
310|
311|“잘 어울리네, 앞으로는 꼭 차고 있어. 그럼 난 이만 정찰조 투입하러 가 봐야겠다.”
312|
313|흡족하게 웃은 원명훈이 성큼성큼 걸음을 옮긴다. 나는 그의 뒷모습이 시야에서 사라지자마자 목걸이를 뺐다.
314|
315|‘진짜 괜찮다니까 그러시네.’
316|
317|원명훈에게는 겸양의 말로 들렸을지 모르지만 나는 있는 그대로의 사실을 말했을 뿐이다.
318|
319|무림에서 임독양맥을 타통하며 [예티의 목걸이]보다 훨씬 좋은 것을 얻었으니까.
320|
321|‘한서불침(寒暑不侵).’
322|
323|그것이 지금까지 땀 한 방울 나지 않은 이유다. 아니, 한 시간이 아니라 열 시간이 지나도 마찬가지다.
324|
325|고작 이 정도 더위로는 내게 아무런 영향도 끼치지 못한다.
326|
327|그런 나보다는 필요한 사람에게 주는 것이 훨씬 낫겠지.
328|
329|“아저씨.”

As I let out an involuntary exclamation, someone came over and tapped me on the shoulder.

[P110]
“Pretty relaxed, aren’t you?”

[P111]
“Oh, Myunghoon hyung. Weren’t you up front?”

[P112]
Our formation had Won Myunghoon in the lead, me in the middle, and Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim bringing up the rear.

[P113]
Won Myunghoon flashed his white teeth in a grin.

[P114]
“You have to check behind you sometimes. Everyone else is struggling, but then I spotted some carefree bastard sightseeing by himself, so I came over.”

[P115]
“What if a wyvern suddenly jumps out?”

[P116]
“We’re still in the jungle zone, so we’ll only run into minor monsters here. Wyverns nest on cliffs and mountain peaks. We’re nowhere near them yet.”

[P117]
“Seriously?”

[P118]
“It’ll take at least half a day to encounter one, or a full day if we’re unlucky. Enjoy the scenery while you can.”

[P119]
I had known higher-level Gates were larger, but I hadn’t expected anything on this scale. I shook my head in disbelief.

[P120]
“This place is incredible. No wonder they give you raid access for a full week.”

[P121]
“That’s how long these raids take. Once you’ve been through a few A-Rank Gates like this, you’ll be sick of them too.”

[P122]
“I don’t know about that.”

[P123]
I probably never would.

[P124]
To me, a Gate had long since stopped being a grueling, tedious workplace. It was a place where I could grow even stronger.

[P125]
“I’m having fun.”

[P126]
“…Well, I suppose that’s possible.”

[P127]
Won Myunghoon gave me an odd look, then handed me something.

[P128]
“Here. Hold on to this.”

[P129]
“What is it?”

[P130]
It was a necklace set with a blue jewel. Before I could inspect the Item, Won Myunghoon continued.

[P131]
“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on. You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later. You’re one of our main combat assets. You need to conserve your strength.”

[P132]
“You don’t have to give me something like this, hyung.”

[P133]
“I’m not giving it to you. I’m lending it to you, so take good care of it and return it later.”

[P134]
Even at a glance, it looked incredibly expensive.

[P135]
I hesitated, but Won Myunghoon kept urging me, so I had no choice but to put it on.

[P136]
Ding.

[P137]
> **System**
> - You have equipped **Yeti’s Necklace**.
> - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.

[P138]
The instant the notification appeared, a chill cold enough to send shivers down my spine enveloped my entire body.

[P139]
“It works well.”

[P140]
“It looks good on you. Keep it on from now on. I need to go deploy the scouting team.”

[P141]
Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away. The moment he disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.

[P142]
*I told him I was fine.*

[P143]
Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.

[P144]
When I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels in the Murim, I had gained something far better than *Yeti’s Necklace*.

[P145]
*Unaffected by Cold and Heat.*

[P146]
That was why I hadn’t shed a single drop of sweat. It wouldn’t matter if one hour became ten.

[P147]
This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.

[P148]
It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.

[P149]
“Uncle.”

[P150]
“Huff, huff. What?”

[P151]
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been walking a few steps ahead, turned around. Sweat poured from his head as if someone had installed a sprinkler on top of it.

[P152]
“Why are you sweating so much? Are you all right?”

[P153]
“…Do I look all right?”

[P154]
“No.”

[P155]
“Then don’t talk to me. I’m dying here.”

[P156]
“You should’ve worn something cooler. Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”

[P157]
“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense. At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”

[P158]
“We can’t have that. You have a wife and children.”

[P159]
I laughed quietly and put the necklace around his neck myself. Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as the cool wind of the snowy plains washed over him.

[P160]
“Huh? What’s this?”

[P161]
“A present. Not that I’m giving it to you, of course. I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”

[P162]
“Whew. I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”

[P163]
Life returned to his exhausted face. Just as Im Kkeokjeong beamed at me—

[P164]
—Peeeeep!

[P165]
A piercing shriek rang out from somewhere.

[P166]
Birds hidden within the dense forest burst into flight, and branches and leaves rained down over everyone’s heads.

[P167]
But no one, including me, paid them any attention.

[P168]
—Kyaaaaaaak!

[P169]
A bloodcurdling cry rang out as an enormous shadow engulfed all twenty-odd people.

[P170]
I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.

[P171]
“Wyvern…”

[P172]
Won Myunghoon had been wrong.

[P173]
Not half a day. Not a full day.

[P174]
After only one hour—

[P175]
It had appeared.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 215

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃215화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|와이번(Wyvern).
  6|
  7|드레이크와 함께 이른바 용족(龍族)으로 분류되는 상위 몬스터 중 하나다.
  8|
  9|비행기보다 거대한 몸체와 단단한 외피를 지닌 데다 뛰어난 지능으로 마법마저 구사할 수 있다.
 10|
 11|말 그대로 작은 드래곤이라 불려도 손색이 없을 정도의 힘.
 12|
 13|3년 전 내가 맞닥트린 그놈은 E급 게이트에서 나올 수도, 나와서도 안 되는 존재였다.
 14|
 15|
 16|
 17|‘캬우우우우!’
 18|
 19|
 20|
 21|메아리처럼 들려오는 괴물의 포효와 함께 감았던 눈을 떴다.
 22|
 23|컴컴하고 습한 동굴이 아닌, 쾌청한 하늘과 낯익은 길드원들의 얼굴이 시야에 들어왔다.
 24|
 25|“진태경 씨. 괜찮습니까?”
 26|
 27|“태경아.”
 28|
 29|걱정이 담긴 말을 건네는 길드원들의 모습에 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴을 폈다.
 30|
 31|“네. 잠깐 속이 울렁거려서. 멀미인가 봐요.”
 32|
 33|“멀미? 네가?”
 34|
 35|절정 고수가, 아니 A급 헌터가 멀미라니. 스스로 생각해도 구차한 변명이다.
 36|
 37|요즘 들어 약간 거리를 두던 송이 씨도 걱정스러운 얼굴로 물어볼 정도였다.
 38|
 39|“치유 마법이라도 걸어 드릴까요?”
 40|
 41|“아뇨. 괜찮아요.”
 42|
 43|나는 마지막 잎새의 주인공처럼 힘없이 웃으며 덧붙였다.
 44|
 45|“저는 송이 씨가 옆에 있는 것만으로도 치유되거든요.”
 46|
 47|“……아, 네.”
 48|
 49|임꺽정이 귓가에 대고 속삭였다.
 50|
 51|“이 자식. 방금 같은 멘트는 도대체 어떻게 생각해 낸 거야?”
 52|
 53|“별로였어요?”
 54|
 55|“아니, 미쳤어. 듣는 순간 온몸에 전류가 흐르더라.”
 56|
 57|그 정도야?
 58|
 59|사실 머리가 텅 비어서 아무 말이나 뱉어 본 건데.
 60|
 61|임꺽정의 말마따나 벼락 맞은 사람처럼 우뚝 굳어 있는 송이 씨를 보니 효과가 있는 것 같기도 하고.
 62|
 63|‘근데 왜 크리티컬 느낌이지.’
 64|
 65|그사이 지끈거리던 관자놀이도, 울렁거리는 속도 가라앉았다.
 66|
 67|깊이 심호흡하던 그때, 우리가 타고 있던 리무진 버스의 문이 열리더니 한 사람이 모습을 드러냈다.
 68|
 69|“다들 도착하셨군요. 그런데…….”
 70|
 71|버스 내부에 흐르는 심상치 않은 공기에 말꼬리를 흐린 원명훈이 최 팀장에게 물었다.
 72|
 73|“혹시 무슨 문제라도 생겼나요?”
 74|
 75|“네. 너무 큰 문제라 이야기 좀 해야겠습니다.”
 76|
 77|단호하게 대답한 최 팀장이 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
 78|
 79|“진태경 씨도 함께요.”
 80|
 81|
 82|
 83|* * *
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|“스타 길드는 진작 왔고. 평화 길드는 왜 안 보여?”
 88|
 89|“잠깐, 저거 진태경 아냐?”
 90|
 91|“맞네. 옆에 원명훈도 있는 거 보니까 확실해.”
 92|
 93|“빨리 찍어. 잠시 후에 인터뷰 딸 준비하고.”
 94|
 95|최 팀장, 원명훈. 마지막으로 나.
 96|
 97|우리 셋은 구석진 곳으로 걸음을 옮겼다. 소식을 듣고 몰려든 기자와 헌터들의 시선에 얼굴이 따갑다.
 98|
 99|마침내 끈질기게 달라붙던 사람들의 시선이 떨어지자, 최 팀장이 굳은 얼굴로 입을 열었다.
100|
101|“갑자기 장소가 변경된 이유가 뭡니까?”
102|
103|“변경이라뇨? 그게 무슨.”
104|
105|“만티코어(Manticore)의 밀림이 오늘 레이드 장소 아니었습니까?”
106|
107|“예? 그럴 리가요. 혹시 지금 계약서 갖고 계십니까?”
108|
109|“여기. 정확히 명시되어 있습니다.”
110|
111|최 팀장이 건넨 계약서를 황급히 살펴본 원명훈의 얼굴이 와락 일그러졌다.
112|
113|“1팀장 이 새끼가.”
114|
115|반응을 보아하니 중간에 착오가 있었던 모양이다.
116|
117|평소답지 않게 몇 마디 욕설을 중얼거린 원명훈이 난처한 기색으로 말했다.
118|
119|“죄송합니다. 저희 쪽 직원이 큰 실수를 했네요. 이거 뭐라 말씀을 드려야 할지.”
120|
121|“실수. 그렇군요.”
122|
123|최 팀장의 건조한 목소리가 이어졌다.
124|
125|“오늘 레이드는 없던 것으로 하는 게 좋겠습니다.”
126|
127|“네?”
128|
129|“다른 곳도 아니고 A급 게이트입니다. 완벽한 준비 없이 진입했다가는 불상사가 생길 수도 있습니다. 그리고…….”
130|
131|짧은 순간, 말꼬리를 흐린 최 팀장의 시선이 나를 스쳤다.
132|
133|그는 이미 내 과거 행적을 조사했다.
134|
135|내가 3년 전 있었던 상동역 변이 게이트 사건의 유일한 생존자라는 것, 또한 그 후유증이 아직 남아 있다는 사실도 알고 있다.
136|
137|“우리 길드원들에게 와이번은 아직 무리입니다. 제의는 감사했습니다만, 이쯤에서 물러나는 게 서로에게 좋겠네요.”
138|
139|“팀장님!”
140|
141|원명훈의 당황 섞인 외침에도 최 팀장의 태도는 칼 같았다.
142|
143|“와이번은 안 됩니다. 적어도 지금은요.”
144|
145|“…….”
146|
147|가만히 상황을 지켜보던 내가 불쑥 입을 연 것은 그때였다.
148|
149|“하죠. 레이드.”
150|
151|“진태경 씨.”
152|
153|“인터넷 기사도 나갈 만큼 나갔고, 기자들도 모여 있는데 여기서 무산되면 뒷말 나오지 않겠어요?”
154|
155|나는 나란히 서 있는 최 팀장과 원명훈의 등 뒤를 빤히 바라봤다.
156|
157|어느새 목에 카메라를 건 기자들이 눈치를 보며 슬금슬금 다가오는 중이었다.
158|
159|‘냄새 하나는 기가 막히게 맡네.’
160|
161|심상치 않은 분위기를 읽고 접근해 오는 게 분명하다.
162|
163|그래서 최 팀장이 뭐라 말하기 전에 재빨리 말을 가로막았다.
164|
165|“그렇다고 제가 딱히 인터넷 기사에 신경 쓰는 건 아니고요. 그냥, 이제 괜찮아서 그래요.”
166|
167|“……정말입니까?”
168|
169|“네.”
170|
171|절반은 진심이고, 나머지 절반은 거짓이다.
172|
173|나는 아직 괜찮지 않다. 지난 3년 동안 늘 똑같은 악몽을 반복했고 놈의 포효와 팀원들의 비명을 기억했다.
174|
175|그러고는 식은땀에 흠뻑 젖어 깨어나 아무렇지 않은 척, 늘 똑같은 하루를 반복해 왔다.
176|
177|하지만 이제는 아니다.
178|
179|“할 수 있어요, 그때의 제가 아니니까.”
180|
181|나는 더 이상 무력하기 짝이 없던 F급 헌터가 아니다. 어디를 가도 당당히 강자라 말할 수 있는 한 사람의 절정 고수이자 A급 헌터다.
182|
183|“그러니까 해도 괜찮습니다. 아니, 하고 싶어요.”
184|
185|나를 빤히 바라보던 최 팀장이 깊은 한숨을 내쉬었다.
186|
187|“그래요, 그럽시다.”
188|
189|잠시 후, 우리는 불길하게 일렁이는 마력의 문 앞에 서 있었다.
190|
191|돌아가는 카메라와 쉴 새 없이 터져 나오는 플래시가 협동 레이드를 시작하는 양 측 길드원들의 모습을 담았다.
192|
193|“후우.”
194|
195|나는 깊은 심호흡과 함께 걸음을 내디뎠다.
196|
197|익숙한 시스템 알림과 함께 끈적한 마력이 몸을 휘감는다.
198|
199|띠링.
200|
201|
202|
203|- A급 게이트, [블랙 와이번의 둥지]에 진입하셨습니다.
204|
205|- 클리어 시 활약에 걸맞은 보상이 지급됩니다.
206|
207|
208|
209|스스스.
210|
211|다시 눈을 뜨자, 주위를 둘러싼 모든 것이 바뀌어 있었다.
212|
213|
214|
215|* * *
216|
217|
218|
219|“후욱. 후우욱.”
220|
221|두꺼운 통짜 갑옷을 걸친 임꺽정의 입에서 단내가 뿜어져 나왔다.
222|
223|게이트에 진입한 지 한 시간, 어느새 그의 이마에는 땀이 비처럼 쏟아져 내리는 중이었다.
224|
225|그것은 비단 임꺽정에게만 해당되는 사안이 아니었다. 스타 길드와 평화 길드. 도합 이십 명이 넘는 인원 중 대부분이 땀을 줄줄 흘리며 걸음을 옮겼다.
226|
227|‘그럴 만도 하지.’
228|
229|나는 혀를 차며 주위를 둘러봤다.
230|
231|이글거리는 태양 아래, 수십 미터가 넘어가는 나무와 괴상하게 생긴 풀들로 형성된 밀림이 끝없이 펼쳐져 있다.
232|
233|이처럼 보기만 해도 숨이 턱 막히는 광경에 습식 사우나보다 뜨겁고 축축한 공기는 화룡점정을 찍었다.
234|
235|‘원시림(原始林).’
236|
237|그야말로 공룡 다큐멘터리에 나올 법한 광경이 눈앞에 펼쳐져 있었다.
238|
239|날씨는 둘째 치고, 보이는 풍경 자체는 장관이라고 할 만했다.
240|
241|“이야.”
242|
243|나도 모르게 감탄사를 흘리고 있던 그때, 한 사람이 다가와 어깨를 툭 쳤다.
244|
245|“여유 있다, 너?”
246|
247|“아, 명훈이 형. 선두에 계신 것 아니었어요?”

I gave her a feeble smile like the protagonist of *The Last Leaf* and added, “Just having you beside me is healing enough, Song-i.”

[P19]
“…Ah. Yes.”

[P20]
Im Kkeokjeong leaned close and whispered in my ear, “You bastard. How the hell did you come up with a line like that?”

[P21]
“Was it bad?”

[P22]
“No, it was insane. The moment I heard it, electricity shot through my whole body.”

[P23]
Was it really that powerful?

[P24]
My mind had been completely blank, so I’d just blurted out the first thing that came to me.

[P25]
But judging by Song-i, who had frozen like someone struck by lightning, it did seem to have worked.

[P26]
*Why does it feel like I landed a critical hit?*

[P27]
Meanwhile, the throbbing in my temples and the nausea in my stomach had both subsided.

[P28]
Just as I took a deep breath, the door of our limousine bus opened and a man appeared.

[P29]
“Everyone’s here. But…”

[P30]
Won Myunghoon trailed off at the tense atmosphere inside the bus, then turned to Team Leader Choi.

[P31]
“Did something happen?”

[P32]
“Yes. Something serious enough that we need to talk.”

[P33]
Team Leader Choi answered firmly, then turned toward me.

[P34]
“You too, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P35]
* * *

[P36]
“The Star Guild got here ages ago. Where’s the Peace Guild?”

[P37]
“Wait, isn’t that Jin Taekyung?”

[P38]
“It is. Won Myunghoon’s beside him, so it’s definitely him.”

[P39]
“Start taking pictures. Get ready to interview him afterward.”

[P40]
Team Leader Choi, Won Myunghoon, and I moved toward a secluded corner.

[P41]
The reporters and Hunters who had flocked here after hearing the news stared so intently that I could feel their gazes burning into my face.

[P42]
Once their persistent attention finally drifted away, Team Leader Choi spoke with a grim expression.

[P43]
“Why was the location suddenly changed?”

[P44]
“Changed? What do you mean?”

[P45]
“Wasn’t Manticore’s Jungle supposed to be today’s raid location?”

[P46]
“What? That can’t be right. Do you have the contract with you?”

[P47]
“Here. It’s stated clearly.”

[P48]
Won Myunghoon hurriedly examined the contract Team Leader Choi handed him. His face twisted.

[P49]
“That bastard, the leader of Team One.”

[P50]
Judging by his reaction, there had been a mistake somewhere along the way.

[P51]
After muttering several curses—unusual for him—Won Myunghoon spoke with an awkward expression.

[P52]
“I’m sorry. One of our employees made a serious mistake. I don’t know what to say.”

[P53]
“A mistake. I see.”

[P54]
Team Leader Choi continued in a dry voice.

[P55]
“I think it would be best to call off today’s raid.”

[P56]
“What?”

[P57]
“This isn’t just any Gate. It’s an A-Rank Gate. Entering without proper preparation could lead to an accident. And…”

[P58]
Team Leader Choi trailed off for a moment, his gaze flicking toward me.

[P59]
He had already investigated my past.

[P60]
He knew I was the sole survivor of the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate incident three years ago. He also knew I was still suffering from the aftereffects.

[P61]
“Wyverns are still too much for our Guild members. We appreciate the offer, but I think it would be best for both sides if we withdrew.”

[P62]
“Team Leader!”

[P63]
Despite Won Myunghoon’s flustered cry, Team Leader Choi’s stance remained firm.

[P64]
“Wyverns are out of the question. At least for now.”

[P65]
“…”

[P66]
That was when I abruptly spoke up after watching the situation in silence.

[P67]
“Let’s do it. The raid.”

[P68]
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”

[P69]
“Plenty of articles have already gone up online, and all these reporters are here. If we call it off now, won’t people start talking?”

[P70]
I stared past Team Leader Choi and Won Myunghoon, who stood side by side.

[P71]
Reporters with cameras hanging from their necks were already watching us carefully as they edged closer.

[P72]
*They’ve got one hell of a nose for a story.*

[P73]
They had clearly sensed the tension and were coming over to investigate.

[P74]
Before Team Leader Choi could say anything, I quickly cut him off.

[P75]
“Not that I particularly care about the articles. I’m saying this because I’m fine now.”

[P76]
“Are you sure?”

[P77]
“Yes.”

[P78]
Half of that was true. The other half was a lie.

[P79]
I still wasn’t fine. For the past three years, I had relived the same nightmare over and over, remembering the creature’s roar and my teammates’ screams.

[P80]
Then I would wake drenched in cold sweat, pretend nothing had happened, and go through another day just like all the others.

[P81]
But not anymore.

[P82]
“I can do this. I’m not the same person I was back then.”

[P83]
I was no longer the utterly powerless F-Rank Hunter I had been. I was a Peak master and an A-Rank Hunter—someone who could stand tall anywhere and call himself strong.

[P84]
“So it’s fine. No, I want to do it.”

[P85]
Team Leader Choi stared at me for a long moment, then let out a deep sigh.

[P86]
“All right. Let’s do it.”

[P87]
A short while later, we stood before a doorway of ominously rippling mana.

[P88]
Rolling cameras and incessant flashes captured the members of both Guilds as we began our joint raid.

[P89]
“Phew.”

[P90]
I took a deep breath and stepped forward.

[P91]
Sticky mana coiled around my body as the familiar System notification appeared.

[P92]
Ding.

[P93]
> **System**
> - You have entered **A-Rank Gate, The Black Wyvern’s Nest**.
> - Upon clearing the Gate, you will receive a Reward commensurate with your performance.

[P94]
Ssshhh.

[P95]
When I opened my eyes again, everything around me had changed.

[P96]
* * *

[P97]
“Huff. Huuuff.”

[P98]
Im Kkeokjeong, clad in heavy full plate armor, panted raggedly.

[P99]
An hour had passed since we entered the Gate, and sweat was already pouring down his forehead like rain.

[P100]
He wasn’t the only one. Most of the more than twenty members of the Star and Peace Guilds trudged along with sweat streaming from their bodies.

[P101]
*Hardly surprising.*

[P102]
I clicked my tongue and looked around.

[P103]
Beneath the blazing sun, a jungle of trees dozens of meters tall and bizarre-looking plants stretched endlessly into the distance.

[P104]
The sight alone was suffocating, and air hotter and more humid than a steam sauna completed the picture.

[P105]
*A primeval forest.*

[P106]
It looked exactly like something out of a dinosaur documentary.

[P107]
The weather aside, the scenery itself was spectacular.

[P108]
“Wow.”

[P109]
As I let out an involuntary exclamation, someone came over and tapped me on the shoulder.

[P110]
“Pretty relaxed, aren’t you?”

[P111]
“Oh, Myunghoon hyung. Weren’t you up front?”

[P112]
Our formation had Won Myunghoon in the lead, me in the middle, and Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim bringing up the rear.

[P113]
Won Myunghoon flashed his white teeth in a grin.

[P114]
“You have to check behind you sometimes. Everyone else is struggling, but then I spotted some carefree bastard sightseeing by himself, so I came over.”

[P115]
“What if a wyvern suddenly jumps out?”

[P116]
“We’re still in the jungle zone, so we’ll only run into minor monsters here. Wyverns nest on cliffs and mountain peaks. We’re nowhere near them yet.”

[P117]
“Seriously?”

[P118]
“It’ll take at least half a day to encounter one, or a full day if we’re unlucky. Enjoy the scenery while you can.”

[P119]
I had known higher-level Gates were larger, but I hadn’t expected anything on this scale. I shook my head in disbelief.

[P120]
“This place is incredible. No wonder they give you raid access for a full week.”

[P121]
“That’s how long these raids take. Once you’ve been through a few A-Rank Gates like this, you’ll be sick of them too.”

[P122]
“I don’t know about that.”

[P123]
I probably never would.

[P124]
To me, a Gate had long since stopped being a grueling, tedious workplace. It was a place where I could grow even stronger.

[P125]
“I’m having fun.”

[P126]
“…Well, I suppose that’s possible.”

[P127]
Won Myunghoon gave me an odd look, then handed me something.

[P128]
“Here. Hold on to this.”

[P129]
“What is it?”

[P130]
It was a necklace set with a blue jewel. Before I could inspect the Item, Won Myunghoon continued.

[P131]
“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on. You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later. You’re one of our main combat assets. You need to conserve your strength.”

[P132]
“You don’t have to give me something like this, hyung.”

[P133]
“I’m not giving it to you. I’m lending it to you, so take good care of it and return it later.”

[P134]
Even at a glance, it looked incredibly expensive.

[P135]
I hesitated, but Won Myunghoon kept urging me, so I had no choice but to put it on.

[P136]
Ding.

[P137]
> **System**
> - You have equipped **Yeti’s Necklace**.
> - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.

[P138]
The instant the notification appeared, a chill cold enough to send shivers down my spine enveloped my entire body.

[P139]
“It works well.”

[P140]
“It looks good on you. Keep it on from now on. I need to go deploy the scouting team.”

[P141]
Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away. The moment he disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.

[P142]
*I told him I was fine.*

[P143]
Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.

[P144]
When I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels in the Murim, I had gained something far better than *Yeti’s Necklace*.

[P145]
*Unaffected by Cold and Heat.*

[P146]
That was why I hadn’t shed a single drop of sweat. It wouldn’t matter if one hour became ten.

[P147]
This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.

[P148]
It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.

[P149]
“Uncle.”

[P150]
“Huff, huff. What?”

[P151]
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been walking a few steps ahead, turned around. Sweat poured from his head as if someone had installed a sprinkler on top of it.

[P152]
“Why are you sweating so much? Are you all right?”

[P153]
“…Do I look all right?”

[P154]
“No.”

[P155]
“Then don’t talk to me. I’m dying here.”

[P156]
“You should’ve worn something cooler. Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”

[P157]
“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense. At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”

[P158]
“We can’t have that. You have a wife and children.”

[P159]
I laughed quietly and put the necklace around his neck myself. Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as the cool wind of the snowy plains washed over him.

[P160]
“Huh? What’s this?”

[P161]
“A present. Not that I’m giving it to you, of course. I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”

[P162]
“Whew. I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”

[P163]
Life returned to his exhausted face. Just as Im Kkeokjeong beamed at me—

[P164]
—Peeeeep!

[P165]
A piercing shriek rang out from somewhere.

[P166]
Birds hidden within the dense forest burst into flight, and branches and leaves rained down over everyone’s heads.

[P167]
But no one, including me, paid them any attention.

[P168]
—Kyaaaaaaak!

[P169]
A bloodcurdling cry rang out as an enormous shadow engulfed all twenty-odd people.

[P170]
I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.

[P171]
“Wyvern…”

[P172]
Won Myunghoon had been wrong.

[P173]
Not half a day. Not a full day.

[P174]
After only one hour—

[P175]
It had appeared.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
